title: Explicit and implicit waits and custom conditions

videos.script: A test that sleeps for two seconds is making a guess about the future. {{sleep}} This lesson replaces that guess with a question the page can answer. {{suite}} You start with four tests full of sleeps. One sleep is too short, and its test fails. Make it longer and the suite passes, taking twice the time it needs. {{implicit}} Then Selenium's implicit wait. It waits for an element to exist, and for nothing else. A button that exists but does nothing yet is clicked at once, and the click is lost. {{explicit}} An explicit wait asks a condition again and again, until it holds or the time runs out. {{custom}} When no ready-made condition fits, you write your own. A function in the page, a question to the server, or a block of checks retried together. {{timeouts}} Every wait has a timeout, and Playwright has several layers of them. You read the real defaults out of the installed code. Then you watch a raised timeout pass a shop that got six seconds slower. {{toast}} Last, a wait that arrives too late. The shop's message lasts two seconds. A test that looks after that fails, whatever its timeout says. Waiting longer cannot bring back a state that has gone. {{end}}
